content.title: De-escalation from potent P2Y12 inhibitor to clopidogrel
content.summary: Discussion of strategies to switch oral P2Y12 receptor inhibitors (e.g., prasugrel/ticagrelor to clopidogrel) in patients with acute coronary syndromes (ACS) to reduce bleeding risk, with caution about potential increased ischemic events early after ACS. Genotype-guided de-escalation using CYP2C19 testing and guided de-escalation using platelet-function testing have been evaluated in randomized trials.
recommendations: Consider switching between oral P2Y12 receptor inhibitors in selected cases (bleeding complications, side effects, socioeconomic factors).

De-escalation to clopidogrel may be considered as an alternative to default regimens to reduce bleeding risk, but is not recommended in the first 30 days after the index ACS event due to potential increased ischemic risk.

Genotype-guided de-escalation (CYP2C19-guided) within 48 hours of PPCI was non-inferior to standard ticagrelor/prasugrel therapy at 12 months for thrombotic events and reduced bleeding in the cited trial.

key_trials.name: MASTER DAPT
key_trials.finding: Abbreviated DAPT (1 month) followed by aspirin or P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy vs standard therapy showed comparable net adverse clinical events; abbreviated therapy reduced major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding.

key_trials.name: TROPICAL-ACS
key_trials.finding: Platelet-function-test–guided de-escalation from prasugrel to clopidogrel at 2 weeks post-ACS was non-inferior to standard prasugrel at 1 year for net clinical benefit.

key_trials.name: POPular Genetics (CYP2C19 genotype-guided)
key_trials.finding: CYP2C19-genotype–guided de-escalation from ticagrelor/prasugrel to clopidogrel in ACS patients undergoing PPCI within 48 h was non-inferior for thrombotic events at 12 months and resulted in lower bleeding.

key_trials.name: TOPIC
key_trials.finding: Unguided de-escalation in 645 ACS patients from ticagrelor/prasugrel to clopidogrel after 1 month reduced adverse clinical and bleeding events with unchanged ischemic endpoints.

key_trials.name: TALOS-AMI
key_trials.finding: Unguided de-escalation in stabilized ACS patients from ticagrelor to clopidogrel after 1 month of DAPT showed significant 12-month reductions in net outcomes.

practical_notes: Switching decisions may be influenced by bleeding complications, dyspnoea on ticagrelor, allergic reactions, and socioeconomic factors.
Platelet-function testing or CYP2C19 genotyping can guide de-escalation in selected patients.
Avoid de-escalation within the first 30 days after the index ACS event when possible because of increased ischemic risk.

Associated Conditions: Bleeding risk related to P2Y12 inhibitor use
Response to P2Y12 receptor inhibitors (clopidogrel, prasugrel, ticagrelor)
